notes: THE WARNINGS NOW TELL THE TRUTH, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A warning that appears when nothing is wrong is not a small thing: you clear it, it returns, and before long you stop reading that panel — which is where the warnings that DO matter are also written. This release is a sweep for exactly that, and it began with one found on our own machine. BACKUPS IN ONEDRIVE ARE NOW RECOGNISED AS BEING IN ONEDRIVE. If your backup folder is the one modern macOS creates — named for your account, like OneDrive-Personal — the app could not tell it was a cloud folder at all. Two things followed, and the second matters more: it told you your backups were "on this same computer" when they were not, and it stayed SILENT about the fact that your complete ledger, salaries included, was sitting readable in that cloud account with no passphrase. That warning now appears when it should. Google Drive on Windows, which appears as its own drive letter, is recognised too. ON WINDOWS, THE DISK-ENCRYPTION WARNING HAD NEVER ONCE APPEARED. The app asked Windows whether BitLocker was on and misread every answer it could be given, so it always concluded "cannot tell" and said nothing. This product is honest that its real protection is your computer's own login and disk encryption — the app password does not protect the files themselves — so that was the single warning that most needed to work. IF YOUR BACKUP SETTINGS CANNOT BE READ, THE APP NOW SAYS SO, instead of announcing that backups are off and inviting you to set them up again. Doing that would have overwritten a stored passphrase that may still be recoverable, and it was being suggested to people whose backups were running perfectly well. A LEDGER COPIED TO A SECOND COMPUTER is now noticed by the computer's name: the warning about the same books being open in two places relied on a marker that travels with the files when a whole profile is copied — the very case it exists to catch. And restoring a backup no longer makes the app claim that none has been tested. EVERY ACCOUNT FIELD NOW HAS A NAME. Every account, vendor, bank, unit and project field sits under a heading you can read — "Pay from bank", "Expense account". Reading software could not see those headings and announced 123 of these fields as nothing at all. They now take their name from the heading you see, so what is read aloud and what is printed can never drift apart. NO DATABASE CHANGE: your data and settings are untouched and you install straight over the old version. Back up first as a habit — Backup & Export, Back up now.
